provenance.install: cargo install vaultlint, version 0.1.1, built and run inside a container
provenance.install_documented_at: the crate's own page and repository README
provenance.note: Released July 2026; 52 crates.io downloads in its entire history. A weak popularity signal recorded in docs/SCANNERS.md, not a quality judgement.

command: vaultlint scan --fail-on never {mount} >&2; vaultlint scan --format json --fail-on never {mount}
run.invocation_evidence: Recovered on 2026-09-01 from the committed corpus-2 artefacts, not from memory: raw/vaultlint-c2-2026-09-01/<leaf>.stdout.log is vaultlint's human formatter and raw/vaultlint-c2-2026-09-01/<leaf>.json is the same scan under --format json. Those two files are the two halves of the command above. The image is not rebuilt: vaultlint-runner:local still carries the id the 2026-08-31 run used, so a difference in a result is a difference in the corpus and not in a dependency resolved afresh.
run.entrypoint_reason: vaultlint has only --format and --fail-on. Its file count is printed by the human formatter and its findings by the json one, and no single argv produces both. Before this the coverage question was answered by a shell script outside the framework, and how it decided ok versus unavailable was itself unrecorded. One `sh -c` runs the tool twice in one container: the human pass to stderr for its own account of what it read, the json pass to stdout for the findings. Nothing is inferred from whether a file appeared.

evidence.means: vaultlint's own count of the files it opened, printed by its human formatter before it analyses them and before it says whether it found anything

findings.message: Account data is deserialised without an owner check

positive_control.sample_source: the shape of raw/vaultlint.json, with one finding substituted for the fix site of the synthetic case

measurements.note: 2 / 11 nominal and real, from 4 findings across 35 files, published 2026-08-31 with no per-run log. Re-run per case, per variant, through the framework on 2026-09-01 against the corpus pinned at commit 24555d044802db4022112a94d6d70e74291a4b6d.

measurements.envelope_note: This file is NOT in vaultlint's own envelope. It was hand-converted into the flat sol-audit shape in 2026-08-31 by a script that was never committed, which is why the declared envelope differs from the tool's. The conversion is unreproducible and that is a defect, not a design choice; it stays declared as sol-audit because that is what the committed bytes are, and pretending otherwise would silently change a published number.
measurements.note: Covers 8 of the 17 valid cases, so run_all reports it `partial` with 8 not-run and a scoreable denominator of 1. It is the row the B7 handover asks to be re-run first. Produced on 2026-09-01 by a per-case shell script whose artefacts are committed under raw/vaultlint-c2-2026-09-01/; that script is where the command in this declaration was read from, so the command is evidence about this row rather than the thing that produced it.
